## 固定收益市場主軸

9月24日美國公債延續跌勢。油價再度大漲、美國經濟活動保持韌性，加上聯準會官員接連警告通膨可能持續，推升長期借貸成本。彭博盤末報導指出，10年期殖利率上升8個基點至5.20%，30年期逼近5.5%，創2004年以來新高。美國財政部雖擴大公債買回規模，實際買進金額卻低於投資人預期；同日$440億的7年期公債標售，得標殖利率更創下該年期2009年恢復發行以來最高紀錄。

賣壓主要集中在最短天期以外的債券，並蔓延至市政債，指標30年期殖利率突破5%。即使融資成本上升，初領失業救濟金人數仍低，新屋銷售也優於預期，聯準會尚未看到需求急遽放緩的明確跡象。海外方面，挪威升息，英國央行兩位副總裁也更傾向支持緊縮。分階段重啟荷莫茲海峽的協商消息一度收斂油價漲幅，卻未扭轉當日能源價格與長債殖利率的升勢。

## 公債買回不如預期，長期融資成本續升

美國財政部此次買回剩餘年期20至30年的公債，實際買進$40.8億，未用足事先公布的$60億上限，結果公布後殖利率隨即上升。Wellington Management投資組合經理人Brij Khurana表示，近期債市賣壓如此沉重，投資人原先期待財政部會買足全額。市場因而不再只看擴大的買回額度，而更在意政府實際從市場移除了多少存續期間風險。

新債發行也必須提供更高殖利率，才能吸引買家。週四$440億的7年期公債標售，得標殖利率為5.085%，高於前次的4.512%。彭博形容需求不如預期，且殖利率是該年期2009年恢復發行以來最高。投資人在前一天5年期標售後，原盼這次標售能獲得買家支持、穩定市場，結果供給壓力仍未消退。

不過，當日並非各年期全面遭到拋售。彭博每日殖利率序列顯示，2年期小降0.8個基點至4.89%，5年期上升5.6個基點至5.06%，30年期上升7.8個基點至5.479%；2年與10年期利差擴大9.3個基點至31.0個基點。10年期實質殖利率上升5個基點至2.82%，損益兩平通膨率增加3.5個基點至2.38%，顯示實質借貸成本與通膨補償同步上升，共同壓低較長天期名目公債價格。

油價是新一波通膨壓力最明確的來源。紐約下午5時固定收益市場收盤時，布蘭特原油期貨報每桶$106.45，上漲3.27%；西德州原油報$94.30，上漲2.32%。歐洲交易時段，伊朗最高領袖的一名軍事顧問警告，若美國或以色列再度攻擊，伊朗可能將衝突擴大至印度洋，布蘭特油價一度升至約$108。

美國交易時段稍晚，消息指出美國與伊朗談判人員正在研議分階段安排，將重啟荷莫茲海峽與解除美國對伊朗港口的經濟封鎖相互配合，油價漲幅一度收斂。實際運輸也有改善，稍稍抵銷衝突升級的疑慮：船舶追蹤資料顯示，過去一週至少有兩艘滿載的卡達液化天然氣船駛出海峽，另有至少兩艘船駛入，是兩個多月以來最頻繁的同類船舶活動。石油交易員並指出，沙烏地阿拉伯自前一週中起，已向亞洲買家出售近1億桶原油，儘管胡塞武裝再度向延布與塔伊夫發射飛彈。運輸量回升仍不足以阻止能源價格當日大幅收高。

美國最新數據則顯示，經濟仍有相當支撐。截至9月19日當週，初領失業救濟金為19.7萬人，低於市場預期的20.1萬人，也略低於修正後前值19.8萬人；截至9月12日的續領人數為171.9萬人，低於預期175.0萬人，略高於修正後前值171.7萬人。新增裁員有限，持續領取救濟金的人數也僅小幅增加。

8月新屋銷售達68.4萬戶，超過預期的62.0萬戶，並高於修正後前值64.3萬戶；月增6.4%，前月修正為減少4.3%。建築許可呈現較弱的營建訊號：8月終值為140.3萬戶，高於預期139.4萬戶，但低於前值143.3萬戶；月減2.1%，降幅小於預期的2.7%，前月則增加4.3%。

新屋銷售改善之際，房貸成本還在上升。9月24日的30年期房貸利率由6.95%升至7.03%，15年期由6.26%升至6.42%。賣方則以降價、延長待售時間因應。Redfin的8月資料顯示，近五分之一掛牌物件曾降價，為2020年開始統計以來同月最高比率。典型物件上市50天才售出，相較之下，近三年前房貸利率逼近8%時為36天。掛牌量達150萬戶，比2023年多46%。新屋成交較強的同時，房市其他部分仍有大幅讓價的情況。

區域製造業也有所改善。堪薩斯市聯準銀行9月綜合指數由10升至14，高於預期的5；製造業指數由17升至20，也高於預期的9。另外，第2季經常帳赤字由修正後的$2,126億擴大至$2,460億，但小於市場預期的$2,550億。勞動、房屋與工廠數據分別提供了不同面向的證據，說明經濟活動仍能承受較高利率。

紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams在倫敦表示，市場預期年底前再升息一次是合理的，但他仍會隨新資訊到來再作判斷。他形容勞動市場穩健，並特別提到能源成本與AI投資帶動的強勁需求。他預期AI未來幾年將提高生產力，但目前貢獻仍小；若技術持續集中在少數大型企業，效益分配也可能不均。至於中性利率，他指出財政政策與更強的成長有向上推力，人口結構則構成向下力量。

今年具有投票權的費城聯準銀行總裁Anna Paulson表示，若經濟走勢符合她的預期，適度進一步緊縮可能合宜。目前基礎通膨指標介於2.5%至3%，朝2%目標下降的進展有限，而產出穩健成長，就業接近充分就業水準，她也看到動能增強的跡象。關稅對消費者物價的影響已減輕，但中東衝突與資料中心建設又增加壓力。她同時強調，薪資成長仍溫和，勞動成本本身並未增加通膨壓力；是否再加強限制，必須在持續通膨與就業風險之間權衡。

克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack另警告，供給衝擊接連出現，將提高通膨心態根深柢固的風險。里奇蒙聯準銀行總裁Tom Barkin則指出，夏季持續存在的成本壓力不只燃料，還包括關稅、科技與醫療，可能使通膨更難消退，迫使政策進一步緊縮。兩人的疑慮均超出當日油價波動。利率交換市場仍完全反映聯準會未來一年將升息三次、每次25個基點。

布魯金斯學會一篇新論文，則從美國經濟結構的改變，解釋油價衝擊為何未必立即使經濟收縮。西北大學的Diego Kanzig、Luca Zanotti與哈佛大學的James Stock發現，美國成為能源淨出口國後，即使部分家庭與企業受損，整體消費、股票估值、經濟活動與就業仍可能受惠。Kanzig認為，若能源衝擊反而帶動經濟擴張，緊縮政策面臨的兩難便會減少，因為升息可同時抑制通膨與過熱。

市政債的拋售更為劇烈。紐約下午3時，指標30年期殖利率上升11個基點至5.07%，10年期上升14個基點至4.01%，兩者均創至少2011年1月以來新高。基金經理人週三將約$34億債券送交市場徵求買價，規模為2020年疫情衝擊以來最大。Peter DeGroot領軍的摩根大通策略團隊週四警告，價格下跌與資金贖回已開始相互強化；截至週三，市政債9月已下跌2.8%。

殖利率升高也引來部分承接。Invesco的Mark Paris表示，殖利率接近5%後，保險公司、銀行與其他跨市場買家更積極參與。目前可見的市政債待發行規模降至約$159億。Belle Haven的Ryan Ciavarelli指出，認購需求難以判斷，使承銷商對推出新案更謹慎；部分發行人暫緩發債，但定價具吸引力的交易仍找得到買家。

美國高收益債利差小幅擴大。LQD當日總報酬為負0.71%，HYG為負0.27%。股市則收復大部分盤中跌幅，標普500指數收跌0.02%，那斯達克100指數收漲0.03%；美元指數上漲0.15%，黃金期貨下跌0.25%。股市尾盤回穩，當日最明顯的價格調整仍集中在利率敏感度較高的固定收益資產。

## 歐洲各國央行升息訊號轉強

挪威央行升息25個基點至4.5%，是今年第二次升息。事前經濟學家意見接近對半，21人中有11人預期升息。總裁Ida Wolden Bache表示，為在合理期間內使通膨回到2%，利率可能需要維持高檔，必要時還會再升。新的利率預測路徑顯示，政策利率將較6月預估在目前水準附近停留更久，之後才逐步下降。

此次決策值得注意之處，在於基礎通膨其實已較預期更明顯降溫。Wolden Bache表示，這項改善並未實質改變中期展望。央行上修至2028年的消費者物價預測，如今預期要到2029年才會回到目標。薪資假設與6月相近，但更強的國際物價壓力及企業能源成本，抵銷了匯率對通膨的抑制效果。Nordea的Kjetil Olsen認為，海外升息預期上升也很重要：挪威若採取較寬鬆立場，可能使挪威克朗走弱。

瑞典央行將利率維持在1.75%，符合受訪18位經濟學家的全數預期，但明顯強化今年升息的指引。央行表示，若經濟與通膨展望不變，將於2026年開始升息。8月時，央行認為今年升息25個基點的機率僅有一半；如今預期的緊縮幅度也超過6月預測。

瑞典成長預測同步上修。經日曆調整後，2026年成長率由1.9%調高至2.6%，2027年由2%調高至2.2%。總裁Erik Thedeen將可能升息與需求復甦相連結；央行則警告，在經濟更強的情況下，石油、電力與燃料價格重新上漲，以及瑞典克朗走弱，可能帶來更大影響。隔夜交換市場反映的11月升息機率由週初約65%升至91%，Handelsbanken與SEB也將升息預測提前至11月。決策公布後，瑞典克朗兌歐元升值約0.4%，至每歐元11.2454克朗。

英國央行原本支持利率不變的陣營也出現鬆動。副總裁Sarah Breeden與Clare Lombardelli在前一週6比3的表決中，都支持將利率維持在3.75%，如今卻表示更傾向緊縮；若兩人改變立場，貨幣政策委員會的多數可能隨之翻轉。作為重要搖擺票的Breeden指出，能源衝擊持續越久、規模越大，產生顯著第二輪效應的可能性越高。她表示，央行對2027年初的短期通膨預測已由3.2%上修至4%或略高。

Lombardelli強調，企業吸收能源成本的能力有限；若成本持續偏高，又沒有明確的通膨降溫或活動轉弱跡象，緊縮便越來越可能。她不贊成對每一次商品價格變動機械式反應，真正需要判斷的是間接的薪資與物價影響是否正在固化。兩位副總裁都認為，第二輪效應形成得比預期慢，因此薪資協議的證據仍是決策關鍵。Swati Dhingra則持較審慎立場，雖承認能源與薪資風險，但面對轉弱的經濟，她傾向等待。市場幾乎完全反映11月升息至4%，並給予12月再升息60%的機率。

歐洲央行的Isabel Schnabel表示，能源中斷持續時間超過最初預期，影響也從石油擴及柴油與天然氣。奧地利央行總裁Martin Kocher另指出，夏季以來信心改善、工業復甦，顯示經濟更有能力承受較高利率。不過，他仍形容情勢脆弱，未承諾再升息，認為應在不施加多餘限制的情況下達成2%通膨目標。彭博盤末市場報導顯示，德國10年期公債殖利率上升4個基點至3.60%，英國同年期上升3個基點至5.38%。

並非所有投資人都認同市場反映的緊縮路徑。Allspring的Lauren Van Biljon認為升息定價過度積極，仍持有2至5年期英國與歐洲公債，但對長天期保持謹慎。CG Asset Management的Emma Moriarty也質疑英國成長展望是否足以支持市場隱含的升息幅度。RBC BlueBay的Mike Bell透過英國殖利率曲線陡峭化部位表達相同看法，但表示油價若改變，可能必須重新評估。對短期利率究竟需要升多少的疑慮，與持有長債所需的風險補償是兩件事；財政舉債仍是長端的另一項考量。

瑞士仍是低利率政策最明顯的例外。瑞士央行維持零利率，但隨瑞郎走弱，撤下了先前更願意干預匯市、抑制瑞郎升值的措辭。總裁Martin Schlegel仍保留匯市干預選項，並表示中期通膨壓力僅略增。8月通膨為0.8%，央行將2026年預測上修至0.7%，之後兩年各為0.8%；經濟成長預估今年為1.5%至2%，2027年約1.5%。瑞郎兌歐元一度貶值0.4%，至每歐元0.9433瑞郎，隨後收復部分跌幅。多數分析師仍預期2028年前不會升息；LB Macro的Luigi Buttiglione則認為，若歐洲央行持續積極緊縮，瑞士12月便可能升息。

歐洲央行另確認一項重要人事變動：Schnabel將於1月4日離任，轉任國際貨幣基金貨幣及資本市場部門主管，早於原訂2027年12月屆滿的任期。她的離開，加上Christine Lagarde與Philip Lane即將卸任，使待補職缺進一步增加。歐洲各國領袖可能在12月將這些任命一併協商。荷蘭總理Rob Jetten週四肯定Klaas Knot的資格，提及他的央行與債務危機處理經驗。接班程序正在加快，但繼任人選尚未選定，Schnabel的職責可能暫由執委會內部重新分配。

## 亞洲調整資金供給與跨境市場管道

日本在三天銀色週假期後恢復交易，海外債市跌勢隨即反映在本地價格。10年期日本公債殖利率上升10個基點至3.075%，創1996年以來最高；5年與20年期各上升約10個基點，分別至2.375%與3.915%。三井住友信託資產管理的Katsutoshi Inadome指出，日本央行最近一次升息有兩票反對，也無人提議更大幅度升息，加深了政策落後於通膨的疑慮。另有報導稱政府考慮將國防支出提高至GDP的3.5%，使長天期債券再面臨一項財源問題。

紐約市場日圓一度貶至每美元159.04日圓，為9月2日以來最低，160關卡再受矚目。澳洲聯邦銀行的Carol Kong表示，若快速貶破該水準，干預風險將明顯增加。澳洲國民銀行的Ray Attrill認為，干預威脅本身可能限制貶勢，但若要效果持久，可能仍需美國參與，並配合日本加快升息。區域其他市場也承壓，澳洲3年期殖利率上升13個基點至5.07%，創2011年5月以來最高；紐西蘭2年期一度上升17個基點，逼近4%。

亞洲新興市場債券波動相對有限，與美國公債的殖利率差距因此拉大。馬來西亞與泰國殖利率週四約上升5個基點。馬來西亞10年期殖利率本週低於美債122個基點，差距為2007年以來最大；泰國低於美債290個基點，印尼高於美債的幅度則縮至196個基點，接近歷史最低。彭博行業研究的Stephen Chiu認為，南韓與泰國等低殖利率、長天期市場，尤其容易受到資金流入減少甚至撤出的衝擊。不過，Lombard Odier的Homin Lee強調，亞洲許多本幣債與美元債的交易仍具韌性，並特別指出印尼與菲律賓較為脆弱。

台灣並未跟隨海外利率上行，而是著手紓解本地資金壓力。央行連續第16天減少可轉讓定存單發行，這段期間累計釋出創紀錄的新台幣1.02兆元，定存單餘額降至新台幣5.67兆元，為2009年以來最低。AI相關資本支出增加融資需求，帶動金融機構8月放款與投資年增率加快至9.43%，創1998年以來最快。一名央行官員表示，減少發行也在因應中秋節、季底及企業營所稅暫繳造成的季節性資金流出。

菲律賓公布今年首筆零售公債的具體條件。9月29日將舉行定價標售，初始規模為300億披索、年期2.5年，之後開放民眾申購至10月7日。持有五檔今年及2027年到期既有債券的投資人，可換入新債；這批既有債券票息介於4.875%至8%，8月底未償餘額為5,830億披索。採用較短年期，可避免政府長期鎖定偏高的長端融資成本，換債則有助處理近期到期償還需求。

香港正籌備規模更大的數位綠色債券交易。知情人士表示，擬議的多幣別發行規模為港幣150億至200億元，約合$19億至$26億，最快週一可能定價，幣別涵蓋美元、港幣、歐元與離岸人民幣，將超過香港按揭證券公司6月等值港幣120億元的交易。政府已與投資人會面，使其代幣化計畫朝另一筆大型發行推進，透過區塊鏈辦理發行、交易與交割。

中國則正研議在2028年前擴充互換通。據熟悉中國外匯交易中心、上海清算所與香港場外結算公司討論的人士透露，新增工具可能包括標準利率互換與標準債券遠期。前者以可轉讓定存單發行利率作為參考，後者連結國家開發銀行與中國農業發展銀行債券。現行互換通採須識別對手方的雙邊報價，並要求簽訂交易對手信用協議；新工具則採集中清算與匿名競價。互換通第2季清算量達人民幣1.7兆元，年增近48%，顯示跨境避險需求持續成長，為擬議擴充提供了基礎。

美國聯準會另提出影響短期政府債券的監管調整。部分穩定幣發行人須以合格準備資產全額支持負債，包括短期國庫券及其他高品質流動資產，另須滿足信用與營運風險的資本要求。另一項提案規範銀行的申請程序，包括提交營運計畫與財務資訊。兩項提案均進入60天意見徵詢期，因此準備資產制度仍屬未來安排，不是立即新增的國庫券買盤。

## 融資條件凸顯個別借款人風險

亞洲航空尋求降低再融資成本，凸顯燃油成本與流動性不足交互作用的風險。公司已收到中東銀行提供的$10億融資方案，但為尋找更低成本的替代來源，延後敲定協議，同時爭取7億馬來西亞令吉的本地融資額度，目標在12月或1月完成再融資。Maybank的Samuel Yin估計，若能將疫情期間及私人信貸借款約11%的成本降至7%至8%，每年可節省約2億令吉利息；他並指出，相關債務並非今年到期。

公司的營運與財務狀況，使這些潛在節省格外重要。6月底總債務為$41億，部分反映航空業務整併入帳，負債超過資產6.06億令吉。現金9.54億令吉僅能覆蓋184億令吉流動負債的約5%，上半年營運又消耗5.82億令吉現金。亞洲航空未對燃油避險，且已連續兩季虧損；花旗本週調降其股票評等，理由是現金與權益緩衝不足以承受另一波燃油衝擊。Tony Fernandes否認正重新協商Ares融資，也反駁出售飛機的相關報導；公司則未回應最近的籌資協商是否反映流動性壓力。

印尼一項主權擔保立即面臨履約考驗。Waskita Karya未能償付週四到期的2021年A系列債券本金7,220億印尼盾，受託銀行Bank Mega已依擔保提出請求。這項擔保無條件且不可撤銷，涵蓋本金、利息與逾期罰款；財政部與國營擔保機構PT Penjaminan Infrastruktur Indonesia須在原定付款日後20個營業日內支付。Waskita另外已為A、B系列債券利息提撥約289億印尼盾。

這似乎是疫情期間擔保計畫涵蓋的債券或伊斯蘭債券首次未如期支付本金，有別於Waskita先前無擔保債務的違約。同為國營營建商的PT PP，也獲准將本週到期的111億印尼盾票息延至2027年支付，並於本月重整對四家國營銀行約18.2兆印尼盾的債務。就Waskita這批有擔保債券而言，付款時程接下來取決於主權擔保請求的履行。

Braskem重整案的股東支持則有了明確界線。Petrobras執行長Magda Chambriard排除提高持股，並表示任何新增出資都必須由其他投資人相應出資。債權人在約$110億債務的協商中，要求Petrobras與IG4 Capital投入$30億。Petrobras主管兼Braskem董事William Franca仍預期能達成避免破產的共識方案，但表示尚未決定注資。Chambriard指出，Petrobras已接手營運監督，IG4負責公司與財務管理；雙方已開始分工，但債權人要求具約束力的注資承諾，仍未談定。

另一些借款人即使面對較高利率，仍繼續推動融資。巴塞隆納足球俱樂部正與投資人洽談由高盛安排、總額3億歐元的投資等級球場債券，分三批、最長30年期，預計10月至11月配售。這是5.1億歐元融資方案的一部分，用於Spotify Camp Nou球場完工、延誤造成的超支及設施擴建。新債預期融資成本為5.75%至6%，其中球場債券接近區間上緣，相較之下，7月出售的媒體收益債券約為5.14%。

整體方案另包含2.1億歐元固定利率媒體收益債券，以西甲與歐洲足總賽事轉播收入支持，其中一半已於7月售出；最長年期10年，本金於到期時償還。球場債券則納入既有專案證券化架構。工程延誤持續限制收入，俱樂部預期2027至2028年賽季上半季將重返規模較小的蒙特惠奇球場。因此，融資不僅要支付完工成本，也要因應球場未能以完整容量營運、收入受限更久的情況。

為KKR與Energy Capital Partners以£57億收購DCC Energy提供融資的銀行，準備明年透過高收益債與基礎建設貸款，向市場出售£36億融資債務。高盛、摩根士丹利與另十家銀行承銷這筆融資，預計待收購案於第1季完成後出售；英國反壟斷審查使銀行可能必須持有這些債務更久。未來數月到明年待出售的收購融資債務已超過$1,380億，這筆交易也在其中。

Reliance Industries考慮最快下週發行最高1,000億印度盧比、AAA評等的10年期本地債券，票息可能為7.90%。相較之下，週三最高評等10年期公司債平均殖利率為7.97%，這項指標9月已上升37個基點，銀行體系剩餘流動性則降至4.2兆盧比。若成行，將是Reliance本月第二次發債，先前已以7.47%借入1,200億盧比、年期5年的資金。

AI相關承諾持續擴張，開發商之間卻開始爭論誰應承擔建設風險。Anthropic與Akamai簽下七年、$116億的運算服務協議，涵蓋中央處理器使用權；Akamai還授予可轉換成770萬股普通股的認股權證。另一方面，據報Oracle向承建其新墨西哥州資料中心的Blue Owl旗下單位發出不可抗力通知，希望在工程延誤時免除付款。這個已遭遇反對聲浪與監管挫折的專案，因而又增加了合約爭議。

美國固定收益市場收盤後，高盛資產管理的Lindsay Rosner表示，公司持有的超大規模雲端業者債券低於基準權重，原因是預期發債供給增加，而非懷疑AI本身。她的評論於紐約下午5時30分發布，指出投資人以新債替換既有持債，將持續構成市場壓力。穆迪估計這些業者的表外義務接近$3兆，也提醒投資人評估總承諾時，不能只看已發行債券。

墨西哥一筆由世界銀行安排、規模$1.75億的巨災債券，則面臨颶風可能觸發理賠的風險。颶風Polo週四向西北移動，風速約每小時160英里，預報顯示下週初接近下加利福尼亞時風勢可能減弱。債券須同時符合特定地理路徑與中心氣壓門檻，才會觸發理賠。Azimut的Isacco Loconte指出，可能觸發的情境超過70種，對應損失25%至100%；Icosa的Florian Steiger則對目前路徑較不擔憂，並表示投資人需求未退。最終保險損失仍未確定。

歐洲央行氣候事務主管Irene Heemskerk另警告，反覆天災正對供應鏈、生產力與擔保品價值造成累積影響。貝萊德的Louise Kooy-Henckel認為，市場並未充分反映這些長期風險。這不只是單一巨災債券是否觸發的問題：實體損害若一再發生，長期將侵蝕支撐一般債務的收入與資產價值。

## 新興市場政策走向持續分歧

墨西哥央行連續第三次會議將政策利率維持在6.5%，符合受訪23人全數預測，但刪除了暗示將維持此水準的措辭，改為強調未來決策將考量通膨、經濟閒置程度、預期與匯率傳遞效果。9月上半月通膨為3.42%，略高於預期，核心通膨為3.79%；央行也判斷第3季成長可能已放緩。決策公布後，披索擴大跌幅，墨西哥城下午2時15分約報每美元17.75披索。

渣打銀行的Dan Pan認為，更重視匯率傳遞效果，反映央行對與聯準會利差縮小的戒心；若披索走弱威脅通膨，未來可能保留升息空間。Invex的Ricardo Aguilar與Efren Mendez則有不同預測：今年剩餘時間通膨預計低於4%，成長又弱，即使聯準會12月升息，墨西哥央行也不會跟進。燃油補貼已減輕墨西哥的能源衝擊，但部分負擔轉由公共財政承受。

巴西央行將2026年成長預測由6月的2%下修至1.8%，並預估2027年進一步放緩至1.4%。貨幣政策報告估計，第2季產出缺口為0.5%，第3季為0.4%，到2028年第1季將降至負0.4%。信貸正在放緩，所得轉弱，就業僅小幅成長，儘管勞動市場仍偏緊。農業則面臨投入成本高、農民負債及強烈聖嬰現象帶來的氣候風險。

總裁Gabriel Galipolo表示，持續放緩的證據正如預期增加，但警告不宜從單一數據推論整體趨勢。經濟政策主管Paulo Picchetti強調預測的不確定性，同時表示央行不預期2027年會出現明顯衰退。新預測支持從目前限制性政策進一步寬鬆的可能性，但10月4日大選相關的財政不確定性仍未解除。

迦納央行一致決議維持政策利率14%，同樣是連續第三次按兵不動。總裁Johnson Asiama將穀物、能源、公用事業與運輸成本，以及美元走強列為通膨風險。通膨由7月的4.6%升至近5%，預計未來幾季將進入6%至10%的目標區間。外匯存底由6月底的$129億降至8月的$111億，反映能源成本增加與黃金局暫停出口。出貨已在前一週恢復，Asiama預期這將有助回補存底。

奈及利亞最新標售顯示，先前大幅降息正迅速傳導至融資成本。週三售出的182天期國庫券總額395億奈拉，殖利率15.8%；一年期總額4,470億奈拉，殖利率15.89%，兩者均為今年最低。一年期投標需求為售出金額的9.2倍，是2025年6月以來最強，短天期投標倍數則為2.08倍。週三本地公債平均殖利率下降3.2個百分點至15.9%。不過，Meristem的Matilda Adefalujo預期，央行會避免自身用於流動性管理的票券利率過度下降，以維持投資誘因。

智利已就首次瑞郎主權債發行展開投資人洽談，擬由法國巴黎銀行與蘇黎世州銀行安排多批次發售，將是政府今年第三次進入國際債市。7月歐元債交易前公布的海外借款額度，目前仍約有$16億可用。新增幣別可拓展主權融資管道，但最終規模與定價尚未確定。

知情人士表示，沙烏地阿拉伯公共投資基金正考慮先委託Pimco管理$5億，主要投資波斯灣政府債券，尚未做出最終決定。該基金的投資組合以股票、私募資產與國內專案為主，這筆配置將增加固定收益部位。戰爭已使投資人對波斯灣主權債要求的額外殖利率增加121個基點，期間卡達與阿拉伯聯合大公國債券分別虧損5.7%與4.3%。

## 後續市場觀察重點

9月25日公布的耐久財訂單，將檢視區域製造業的強勢是否延伸至實際資本支出承諾。市場預期8月整體訂單月減0.4%，前月為增加1.1%；但扣除運輸的訂單預估增加0.6%，高於前月0.4%，扣除飛機的非國防資本財訂單預估增加0.5%，高於前月0.2%。週四勞動與房屋數據幾乎未顯示總體需求急遽放緩，因此訂單結構格外重要。

同日公布的9月密西根大學調查終值，將提供家庭通膨預期的最新變化，回應Hammack與Barkin對預期升溫的疑慮。市場預期消費者信心為47.6，低於前值51.7；一年期通膨預期為4.6%，高於前值4%，五年期為3.4%，高於前值3.3%。若信心下降而通膨預期上升，將反映家庭承受的壓力，與近期活動數據展現的韌性有所不同。9月30日公布的8月核心PCE則提供更直接的通膨觀察，預測月增0.3%、年增3.4%，前值分別為0.2%與3.3%。

能源外交的焦點已轉向荷莫茲海峽重啟與美國解除封鎖的先後安排。近期液化天然氣船運與沙國售油改善，仍未阻止油價再次大漲。可行的協議必須能在軍事行動可能擴大的威脅下，維持實際運輸。週五亞洲早盤、台北時間上午7時15分前，紐西蘭債券已下跌，澳洲公債期貨也預示將續跌，週四的壓力正延伸至下一個交易時段。

除了總體數據，個別發行人的期限同樣重要。據Valor Economico旗下Pipeline報導，Braskem預計週五向董事會提交新的反提案，而其他股東相應出資已成為Petrobras明確的支持條件。Waskita擔保請求須在20個營業日的期限內付款。香港最快週一的數位債券定價，以及菲律賓9月29日的零售公債標售，將在全球殖利率升高之際確立融資條件；颶風Polo的路徑變化，則將決定墨西哥的或有保險保障是否啟動。

布蘭特原油在固定收益市場收盤時報$106.45，上漲3.27%。分階段重啟荷莫茲海峽的討論曾短暫收斂油價漲幅，卻未扭轉漲勢。初領失業救濟金19.7萬人、新屋銷售68.4萬戶，進一步顯示需求韌性。John Williams認為年底前聯準會再升息一次的預期合理，Anna Paulson則表示適度進一步緊縮可能合宜；利率交換市場完全反映未來一年將升息三次、每次25個基點。

調整不只發生在美債。隨拋售與贖回加劇，紐約下午3時30年期市政債殖利率已達5.07%。挪威將政策利率升至4.5%，英國央行副總裁Sarah Breeden與Clare Lombardelli也更傾向支持緊縮，儘管能源衝擊的第二輪效應形成速度慢於預期。美股收復大部分盤中跌幅，最明顯的壓力仍集中在利率敏感度較高的固定收益資產。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries extended their selloff on September 24 as another surge in oil, resilient U.S. activity and fresh Federal Reserve warnings about persistent inflation pushed long-term borrowing costs higher. The 10-year yield rose 8 basis points to 5.20% in Bloomberg's late-session account, while the 30-year approached 5.5%, its highest since 2004. An expanded Treasury buyback purchased less debt than investors had expected, and a $44 billion seven-year auction required the highest yield since that maturity was reintroduced in 2009.

The pressure was concentrated beyond the shortest maturities and spread into municipal debt, where benchmark 30-year yields crossed 5%. New unemployment claims remained low and home sales exceeded expectations, giving the Fed little evidence of an abrupt demand slowdown even as financing costs rose. Overseas, Norway increased rates and two Bank of England deputy governors moved closer to supporting tightening. Renewed discussion of a phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz briefly moderated oil's advance, but did not reverse the day's rise in energy prices or long yields.

## Treasury Purchases Fall Short as Borrowing Costs Climb

The Treasury accepted $4.08 billion of securities in its buyback of debt maturing in 20-30 years, below the $6 billion maximum announced for the operation. Yields rose after the result. Wellington Management portfolio manager Brij Khurana said investors had expected the department to use the full amount after the severity of the recent selling. The disappointing take-up shifted attention from the enlarged purchase ceiling to how much duration the government was actually removing from the market.

New issuance also required substantial compensation. Thursday's $44 billion seven-year note auction cleared at 5.085%, compared with 4.512% at the previous sale. Bloomberg described demand as weaker than expected and the yield as the highest since the tenor returned in 2009. The result prolonged the supply pressure rather than providing the stabilizing reception investors had sought after the preceding day's five-year sale.

The curve's daily shape differed from an indiscriminate selloff. Bloomberg's daily yield series showed the two-year edging down 0.8 basis point to 4.89%, while the five-year rose 5.6 basis points to 5.06% and the 30-year increased 7.8 basis points to 5.479%. The 2s10s spread widened 9.3 basis points to 31.0. At 10 years, the real yield rose 5 basis points to 2.82%, while inflation compensation increased 3.5 basis points to 2.38%. Both real borrowing costs and inflation compensation contributed to the pressure on longer nominal debt.

Oil supplied the clearest renewed inflation impulse. Brent futures stood at $106.45 a barrel at the 5 p.m. New York fixed-income close, up 3.27%, and WTI at $94.30, up 2.32%. During European trading, Brent had reached about $108 after a military adviser to Iran's supreme leader warned that another U.S. or Israeli attack could lead Tehran to extend the conflict into the Indian Ocean.

Later in the U.S. session, reports that American and Iranian negotiators were exploring a phased arrangement briefly reduced oil's gains. The possible agreement would pair reopening Hormuz with lifting Washington's economic blockade of Iranian ports. Physical shipments offered some counterweight to escalation fears: ship-tracking data showed at least two laden Qatari LNG carriers leaving the strait over the preceding week and at least two vessels entering, the busiest such traffic in more than two months. Oil traders also reported that Saudi Arabia had sold almost 100 million barrels to Asian buyers since the middle of the previous week, despite renewed Houthi missile attacks on Yanbu and Taif. Those flows had improved, but energy prices still finished sharply higher.

Fresh U.S. releases reinforced the picture of an economy with considerable staying power. Initial unemployment claims were 197,000 in the week ended September 19, below the 201,000 consensus and a revised 198,000 previously. Continuing claims for September 12 were 1.719 million, against expectations of 1.750 million and a revised 1.717 million. The combination showed few new layoffs and only a small increase in the number remaining on benefits.

August new-home sales reached 684,000, exceeding the 620,000 consensus and rising from a revised 643,000. The 6.4% monthly increase followed a revised 4.3% decline. Permits offered a softer construction signal: the final August reading was 1.403 million, above expectations of 1.394 million but below 1.433 million previously. The monthly decline was 2.1%, less severe than the expected 2.7%, after a 4.3% increase.

Housing's better sales result came alongside a further rise in mortgage costs. The September 24 30-year mortgage-rate reading was 7.03%, up from 6.95%, and the 15-year rate increased to 6.42% from 6.26%. Sellers were adjusting through prices and time on the market. Redfin's August figures showed nearly one in five listings had a price reduction, the highest share for that month in records starting in 2020. The typical home spent 50 days on the market, versus 36 when mortgage rates approached 8% almost three years earlier; listings totaled 1.5 million, 46% more than in 2023. Stronger new-home transactions therefore coexisted with substantial concessions elsewhere in housing.

Regional manufacturing improved as well. The Kansas City Fed's September composite index rose to 14 from 10, compared with a forecast of 5, while its manufacturing index increased to 20 from 17 against a forecast of 9. Separately, the Q2 current-account deficit widened to $246 billion from a revised $212.6 billion, although it was smaller than the $255 billion consensus. The labor, housing and factory observations added distinct evidence of activity holding up under higher rates.

New York Fed President John Williams said expectations of another increase by year-end were reasonable, while reserving judgment as further information arrived. Speaking in London, he described the labor market as solid and highlighted both energy costs and strong demand associated with AI investment. He expected AI to lift productivity in coming years, but said its contribution was still small and that gains might be unevenly distributed if the technology remained concentrated among a few large companies. On the neutral rate, he described competing forces: fiscal policy and stronger growth pulling upward, demographics pulling downward.

Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson, a voter this year, said modest further tightening could be appropriate if the economy developed as she expected. Underlying inflation measures were running at 2.5%-3% with little progress toward 2%, while output was growing solidly and employment was near full capacity. She saw signs of increasing momentum. Tariff effects on consumer prices had eased, but the Middle East conflict and data-center construction were adding pressure. Her qualification was that wage growth remained modest: labor costs were not themselves adding inflationary pressure. She framed additional restraint as a balance between persistent inflation and risks to employment.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack separately warned that successive supply shocks increased the danger of an inflationary mindset taking hold. Richmond's Tom Barkin identified a broader set of persistent summer costs, including tariffs, technology, fuel and health care, as reasons inflation could become entrenched and tighter policy necessary. Their remarks expanded the concern beyond the day's oil move. Swaps continued to fully price three quarter-point Fed increases over the following year.

A new Brookings paper offered a different explanation for why an oil shock need not bring an immediate U.S. contraction. Northwestern's Diego Kanzig and Luca Zanotti and Harvard's James Stock found that the country's position as a net energy exporter had changed the aggregate response: consumption, equity valuations, activity and employment could benefit even though particular households and businesses suffered. Kanzig argued that an expansionary energy shock would make monetary tightening less conflicted, because it could restrain both inflation and overheating. The finding concerns the economy's changed structure, not a measurement of Thursday's response.

Municipal bonds experienced more acute selling. At 3 p.m. New York time, benchmark 30-year yields were up 11 basis points at 5.07%, and 10-year yields had climbed 14 basis points to 4.01%, both the highest since at least January 2011. Managers put about $3.4 billion of bonds out for bid Wednesday, the most since the pandemic disruption in 2020. JPMorgan strategists led by Peter DeGroot warned Thursday that losses and withdrawals were beginning to reinforce each other, after a September decline of 2.8% through Wednesday.

Higher yields were attracting some offsetting demand. Invesco's Mark Paris said insurers, banks and other crossover buyers had become more active around the 5% threshold. The visible calendar of prospective municipal issuance fell to about $15.9 billion. Belle Haven's Ryan Ciavarelli said underwriters were becoming more cautious about launching deals when order books were difficult to judge, and some issuers were pausing while attractively priced transactions still found buyers.

U.S. high-yield spreads widened modestly. LQD's daily total return was minus 0.71%, compared with minus 0.27% for HYG. Equities recovered much of their intraday decline: the S&P 500 finished down 0.02% and the Nasdaq 100 up 0.03%. The Dollar Index rose 0.15%, while gold futures fell 0.25%. The steadier equity finish left the day's most pronounced adjustment in longer-duration fixed income.

## European Central Banks Strengthen the Tightening Signal

Norway delivered a quarter-point increase to 4.5%, its second rise this year, after a closely divided economist survey in which 11 of 21 expected a hike. Governor Ida Wolden Bache said rates would probably need to stay elevated and could rise further if necessary to return inflation to 2% within a reasonable period. Norges Bank's projected path remained close to the new level for longer than envisaged in June before eventually declining.

The decision was notable because underlying inflation had moderated more than expected. Wolden Bache said that improvement had not materially changed the medium-term outlook. The bank raised consumer-price forecasts through 2028 and now expected inflation to reach target only in 2029. Wage assumptions were similar to June's, but stronger international price pressures and firms' energy costs were working against the restraining effect of the exchange rate. Nordea's Kjetil Olsen said higher rate expectations abroad also mattered: a softer Norwegian stance risked weakening the krone.

Sweden held its rate at 1.75%, as all 18 surveyed economists expected, but moved its guidance substantially toward an increase this year. The Riksbank said hikes would begin in 2026 if the economic and inflation outlook remained unchanged. In August, it had assigned an even chance to a quarter-point increase this year. It now expected more tightening than in its June projections.

The revision accompanied stronger growth forecasts. Calendar-adjusted expansion was raised to 2.6% for 2026 from 1.9%, and to 2.2% for 2027 from 2%. Governor Erik Thedeen linked the prospective increase to recovering demand, while the bank warned that renewed oil, electricity and fuel inflation and a weaker krona could have larger effects in a stronger economy. Overnight swaps put the chance of a November increase at 91%, versus about 65% at the week's start. Handelsbanken and SEB brought their calls forward to November, and the krona rose about 0.4% against the euro to 11.2454 following the decision.

Britain's policy coalition also shifted. Deputy governors Sarah Breeden and Clare Lombardelli, both of whom had supported holding at 3.75% in the previous week's 6-3 vote, signaled they were moving toward tightening. A change by both could alter the Monetary Policy Committee's majority. Breeden, an important swing voter, said the longer and larger the energy shock became, the more likely it was to generate material second-round effects. The bank's short-term inflation forecast for early 2027 had risen from 3.2% to 4% or slightly above, she said.

Lombardelli emphasized that companies' ability to absorb energy costs was limited. Tightening was increasingly likely if those costs persisted without clear evidence of disinflation or weaker activity. She cautioned against mechanically responding to every commodity-price change; the issue was whether indirect effects on wages and prices were becoming embedded. Both deputies said second-round effects had developed more slowly than expected, leaving wage-settlement evidence important to their decisions. Swati Dhingra offered a counterweight, acknowledging energy and wage risks but indicating she would wait in the face of a weakening economy. Markets were almost fully pricing a November increase to 4% and assigned a 60% chance to another move in December.

The ECB's Isabel Schnabel said the energy disruption was lasting longer than initially anticipated and extending across diesel and gas as well as oil. Austrian central-bank chief Martin Kocher independently pointed to improving sentiment and industrial recovery since the summer, suggesting the economy had more capacity to withstand higher rates. He nevertheless called the situation fragile and declined to commit to another increase, preferring to achieve 2% inflation without unnecessary restraint. German 10-year yields rose 4 basis points to 3.60% in Bloomberg's late market account; the comparable gilt yield increased 3 basis points to 5.38%.

Not all investors accepted the tightening path embedded in those markets. Allspring's Lauren Van Biljon retained exposure to two- to five-year British and European government debt, judging rate pricing too aggressive while remaining cautious on long maturities. CG Asset Management's Emma Moriarty similarly questioned whether Britain's growth outlook justified the implied increases. RBC BlueBay's Mike Bell expressed that view through a UK curve-steepening position, but said a change in oil prices could force a reassessment. The distinction was between the amount of short-rate tightening and the compensation required to hold long debt, where fiscal borrowing remained a separate concern.

Switzerland remained the clearest low-rate exception. The SNB held at zero, but removed its heightened willingness to intervene against franc appreciation as the currency weakened. President Martin Schlegel retained the option of currency intervention and said medium-term inflation pressure had increased only slightly. August inflation was 0.8%; the bank raised its forecasts to 0.7% in 2026 and 0.8% in each of the next two years. It expected growth of 1.5%-2% this year and about 1.5% in 2027. The franc initially fell as much as 0.4% to 0.9433 per euro before recovering part of the decline. Most analysts still expected no rate increase before 2028, contrasting with LB Macro's Luigi Buttiglione, who saw December as possible if the ECB continued tightening aggressively.

The ECB also confirmed an important personnel change: Schnabel will leave to head the IMF's monetary and capital markets department on January 4, before her term's scheduled conclusion in December 2027. Her departure adds another vacancy to the coming exits of Christine Lagarde and Philip Lane. European leaders may negotiate the appointments together in December. Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten backed Klaas Knot's credentials Thursday, citing his central-bank and debt-crisis experience. The succession process is accelerating, although no replacement has been chosen and Schnabel's responsibilities may temporarily be reassigned within the board.

## Asian Markets Adjust Funding and Market Access

Japan's reopening after the three-day Silver Week holiday brought the overseas bond decline into domestic prices. The 10-year JGB yield rose 10 basis points to 3.075%, the highest since 1996; five- and 20-year yields increased by about 10 basis points each to 2.375% and 3.915%. Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset Management's Katsutoshi Inadome said the two dissents against the BOJ's latest increase and the absence of a proposal for a larger move had reinforced concern that policy was lagging inflation. A reported government consideration of defense spending at 3.5% of GDP added a separate financing question at longer maturities.

The yen weakened as far as 159.04 per dollar in New York, its lowest since September 2, bringing the 160 area back into focus. Commonwealth Bank's Carol Kong said a rapid move through that level would materially increase intervention risk. National Australia Bank's Ray Attrill thought the threat itself might limit depreciation, but argued that lasting effectiveness could depend on U.S. participation and a faster Japanese tightening path. These were conditional assessments, not announcements of a new operation. Elsewhere in the region, Australian three-year yields rose 13 basis points to 5.07%, the highest since May 2011, and New Zealand two-year yields increased as much as 17 basis points to just below 4%.

Emerging Asian bonds moved less dramatically, creating wider differentials against Treasuries. Malaysian and Thai yields rose by about 5 basis points Thursday. Malaysia's 10-year discount to Treasuries reached 122 basis points this week, the largest since 2007, while Thailand's reached 290 basis points; Indonesia's premium narrowed to 196 basis points, near a record low. Bloomberg Intelligence's Stephen Chiu said low-yielding, longer-dated markets such as South Korea and Thailand were particularly exposed to reduced inflows or outright withdrawals. Lombard Odier's Homin Lee nevertheless emphasized the resilience of much Asian local- and dollar-debt trading, while singling out Indonesia and the Philippines as more vulnerable.

Taiwan moved to ease domestic funding pressure rather than mirror the overseas rate move. Its central bank reduced issuance of negotiable certificates of deposit for a 16th consecutive day, releasing a record NT$1.02 trillion of liquidity over that run. Outstanding certificates fell to NT$5.67 trillion, the lowest since 2009. Loan and investment growth at monetary institutions had accelerated to 9.43% in August, the fastest since 1998, as AI-related capital spending increased financing demand. A central-bank official said reduced issuance also addressed seasonal drains from the Mid-Autumn Festival, quarter-end and provisional corporate tax payments.

The Philippines supplied firm terms for its first retail bond offering of the year. A September 29 price-setting auction will offer an initial PHP30 billion of 2.5-year debt, followed by public subscriptions through October 7. Holders of five existing series maturing this year and in 2027 can exchange into the new issue. Those securities carried coupons of 4.875%-8% and had PHP583 billion outstanding at August's end. The short maturity limits the government's commitment to elevated longer-term funding costs, while the exchange offers a way to address near-term redemptions.

Hong Kong was preparing a much larger digital green-bond transaction. People familiar with the plans put the proposed multicurrency sale at HK$15 billion-HK$20 billion, or $1.9 billion-$2.6 billion, potentially pricing as early as Monday. It would include U.S. dollars, Hong Kong dollars, euros and offshore yuan and exceed Hong Kong Mortgage Corp.'s HK$12 billion-equivalent June transaction. The government's meetings with investors move its tokenization program toward another substantial offering, using blockchain for issuance, trading and settlement.

China was separately working on expanding Swap Connect by 2028 to include Standard Interest Rate Swaps and Standard Bond Forwards, according to people familiar with discussions among CFETS, Shanghai Clearing House and OTC Clearing Hong Kong. Standardized swaps use negotiable-certificate issuance rates as their reference; the forwards are linked to China Development Bank and Agricultural Development Bank of China debt. Central clearing and anonymous bidding distinguish the instruments from the current link's identifiable bilateral quotations and required counterparty credit agreements. Swap Connect clearing volume reached CNY1.7 trillion in Q2, nearly 48% higher than a year earlier, giving the proposed additions an already growing cross-border hedging base.

In the United States, the Fed proposed a different regulatory change affecting short-term government debt. Certain stablecoin issuers would have to fully back their liabilities with permitted reserves including short-term Treasury bills and other high-quality liquid assets, alongside capital requirements for credit and operational risks. A separate proposal establishes banks' application process, including business plans and financial information. Both measures enter a 60-day comment period, making the reserve framework prospective rather than an immediate new source of bill purchases.

## New Financing Terms Expose Borrower-Specific Risks

AirAsia's search for cheaper refinancing highlighted the interaction between fuel costs and limited liquidity. The carrier had received a $1 billion financing offer from Middle Eastern banks but was delaying a final agreement while seeking lower-cost alternatives. It was also pursuing MYR700 million of local facilities and aimed to complete refinancing by December or January. Maybank's Samuel Yin estimated annual interest savings of about MYR200 million if the airline could reduce pandemic-era and private-credit borrowing costs from around 11% to 7%-8%. He said the relevant debt did not mature this year.

The operating position makes those prospective savings important. AirAsia had $4.1 billion of total debt at June's end, partly reflecting consolidation of airline businesses, and liabilities exceeded assets by MYR606 million. Cash of MYR954 million covered only about 5% of MYR18.4 billion in current liabilities, while operations consumed MYR582 million in the first half. The unhedged carrier had posted two consecutive quarterly losses. Citi downgraded the shares this week, citing thin cash and equity buffers against another fuel shock. Tony Fernandes denied renegotiating the Ares facility and disputed reporting on aircraft sales; the company declined to address whether its latest fundraising discussions reflected liquidity pressure.

An Indonesian sovereign guarantee faced an immediate test. Waskita Karya could not repay IDR722 billion of principal on its 2021 Series A bonds due Thursday. Trustee Bank Mega submitted a claim under the guarantee, which covers principal, interest and late-payment penalties unconditionally and irrevocably. The Finance Ministry and state guarantor PT Penjaminan Infrastruktur Indonesia have 20 business days after the scheduled payment date to settle. Waskita separately set aside about IDR28.9 billion for interest on Series A and B notes.

The missed principal payment appears to be the first involving bonds or sukuk covered by the pandemic-era program, rather than another default on Waskita's previously unguaranteed debt. Fellow state builder PT PP had also secured approval to defer an IDR11.1 billion coupon due this week to 2027, alongside this month's restructuring of about IDR18.2 trillion owed to four state banks. For the guaranteed Waskita notes, the payment timetable now depends on execution of the sovereign-backed claim.

Braskem's restructuring encountered a clearly stated limit on shareholder support. Petrobras Chief Executive Magda Chambriard ruled out increasing the company's stake and said any fresh contribution must be matched by other investors. Creditors had demanded $3 billion from Petrobras and IG4 Capital in talks over about $11 billion of debt. Petrobras executive and Braskem director William Franca still expected a consensual solution that avoided bankruptcy, but said no capital-injection decision had been made. Chambriard said Petrobras was now overseeing operations while IG4 handled corporate and financial management. The division of responsibilities had begun, but the binding equity support sought by creditors remained unresolved.

Other borrowers advanced financing despite the higher-rate environment. FC Barcelona was discussing EUR300 million of investment-grade stadium bonds across three tranches with maturities up to 30 years, arranged by Goldman Sachs. The prospective October-November placements form part of a EUR510 million package covering completion, delay-related overruns and expanded facilities at Spotify Camp Nou. New notes were expected to cost 5.75%-6%, with stadium debt toward the upper end, compared with around 5.14% on media notes sold in July.

The package also includes EUR210 million of fixed-rate media notes backed by La Liga and UEFA broadcast revenues, half already sold in July, with maturities up to 10 years and principal due at maturity. Stadium notes join the existing project securitization. Construction delays continue to constrain receipts: Barcelona expects to return to the smaller Montjuic venue for the first half of the 2027-2028 season. The financing therefore addresses both completion costs and a longer interruption to full-capacity stadium income.

Banks financing KKR and Energy Capital Partners' GBP5.7 billion DCC Energy takeover were preparing to distribute GBP3.6 billion through high-yield bonds and infrastructure loans next year. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and ten other banks underwrote the package. Distribution is expected after the acquisition's anticipated Q1 completion, with British antitrust review prolonging the potential period on bank balance sheets. The financing joins more than $138 billion of buyout debt awaiting sale over coming months and into next year.

Reliance Industries was considering up to INR100 billion of AAA-rated, 10-year local bonds as early as next week, potentially carrying a 7.90% coupon. That compares with a 7.97% average yield for top-rated 10-year corporate debt Wednesday. The benchmark corporate yield had risen 37 basis points during September, while banking-system surplus liquidity had fallen to INR4.2 trillion. The proposed deal would be Reliance's second this month, following INR120 billion of five-year borrowing at 7.47%.

New AI commitments continued to expand even as developers disputed who should bear construction risk. Anthropic signed an $11.6 billion, seven-year computing agreement with Akamai, covering access to central processing units. Akamai also granted a warrant convertible into 7.7 million common shares. Oracle, meanwhile, reportedly sent a force majeure notice to the Blue Owl unit developing its New Mexico data center, seeking to avoid payments if construction was delayed. That introduces a contractual question for a project already encountering opposition and regulatory setbacks.

After the U.S. fixed-income close, Goldman Sachs Asset Management's Lindsay Rosner said the firm held less hyperscaler debt than its benchmark because of expected issuance, rather than skepticism about AI itself. Her comments, published at 5:30 p.m. New York time, identified replacement of existing holdings by new issues as a continuing market pressure. Moody's estimate of almost $3 trillion in hyperscaler off-balance-sheet obligations added another consideration in assessing total commitments beyond outstanding bonds.

Mexico's $175 million World Bank-arranged catastrophe bond faced a different contingent exposure. Hurricane Polo was moving northwest Thursday with winds around 160 miles per hour, while forecasts suggested a weaker storm near Baja California early next week. The bond requires both a specified geographic path and a central-pressure threshold to trigger. Azimut's Isacco Loconte identified more than 70 possible triggering scenarios with losses of 25%-100%; Icosa's Florian Steiger was less concerned about the current track and said investor demand had not retreated. Neither assessment established the final insured loss.

The ECB's climate chief Irene Heemskerk separately warned that repeated weather shocks were creating cumulative effects on supply chains, productivity and collateral values. BlackRock's Louise Kooy-Henckel argued that markets were not adequately pricing these chronic risks. Their concern extends beyond whether one catastrophe bond triggers: recurring physical damage can erode the income and asset value supporting ordinary debt over longer periods.

## Emerging-Market Policy Paths Continue to Diverge

Mexico held its policy rate at 6.5% for a third meeting, matching all 23 surveyed forecasts, but removed language suggesting that level would be maintained. Banxico instead emphasized inflation, economic slack, expectations and exchange-rate pass-through in future decisions. First-half September inflation was 3.42%, slightly above expectations, with core inflation at 3.79%. The bank also judged that growth probably moderated in Q3. The peso extended losses after the announcement, trading around 17.75 per dollar at 2:15 p.m. Mexico City time.

Standard Chartered's Dan Pan interpreted the increased attention to currency pass-through as caution about a narrowing rate differential with the Fed, potentially leaving room for a future increase if peso weakness threatened inflation. Invex economists Ricardo Aguilar and Efren Mendez disagreed on the likely response: with inflation expected below 4% for the rest of the year and weak growth, they did not expect Banxico to follow even a December Fed hike. Fuel subsidies have softened Mexico's energy shock while transferring part of the burden to public finances.

Brazil's central bank cut its 2026 growth projection to 1.8% from June's 2% and forecast a further slowdown to 1.4% in 2027. Its monetary-policy report put the output gap at 0.5% in Q2 and 0.4% in Q3, declining to minus 0.4% by Q1 2028. Credit was slowing, earnings had weakened and employment was growing only modestly, although the labor market remained tight. Agriculture faced high input costs, producer indebtedness and climate risks associated with a strong El Nino.

Governor Gabriel Galipolo said evidence of a sustained slowdown was increasing in line with expectations, but warned against extrapolating individual releases. Economic Policy Director Paulo Picchetti stressed uncertainty in forecasting while saying the bank did not expect a significant recession in 2027. The new projections support the possibility of further easing from the current restrictive stance without resolving the fiscal uncertainty around the October 4 election.

Ghana unanimously held its policy rate at 14%, also for a third meeting, as Governor Johnson Asiama identified grain, energy, utility and transport costs and a stronger dollar as inflation risks. Inflation had risen to almost 5% from July's 4.6% and was expected to enter the 6%-10% target band in coming quarters. Reserves declined to $11.1 billion in August from $12.9 billion at June's end, reflecting energy costs and a temporary halt to Gold Board exports. Shipments resumed the previous week, which Asiama expected to help rebuild reserves.

Nigeria's latest auction showed how quickly its earlier large policy cut was passing into financing costs. At Wednesday's sale, 182-day bills totaling NGN39.5 billion yielded 15.8%, while NGN447 billion of one-year debt yielded 15.89%, the lowest rates of the year. Demand for the one-year bills was 9.2 times the amount sold, the strongest since June 2025; the shorter issue attracted 2.08 times coverage. The average local sovereign-bond yield fell 3.2 percentage points to 15.9% Wednesday. Meristem's Matilda Adefalujo nevertheless expected the central bank to resist excessive declines in rates on its own liquidity-management bills to preserve investor incentives.

Chile began investor discussions for its first Swiss-franc sovereign offering, a prospective multitranch sale arranged by BNP Paribas and Zurcher Kantonalbank. It would be the government's third international-market visit this year. Roughly $1.6 billion remained from the external borrowing amount indicated before July's euro transaction. The new currency broadens the funding channels available to the sovereign without yet establishing final size or pricing.

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund was considering an initial $500 million mandate for Pimco, chiefly in Gulf government bonds, according to people familiar with the discussions. No final decision had been made. The prospective allocation would add fixed-income exposure to a portfolio dominated by equities, private assets and domestic projects after the war had raised the additional yield demanded on Gulf sovereign debt by 121 basis points. Qatar and UAE bonds had suffered losses of 5.7% and 4.3%, respectively, over that period.

## Forward Market Significance

September 25 durable-goods orders will test whether the strength in regional manufacturing extends to actual capital commitments. Consensus expects August orders down 0.4% after a 1.1% rise, but orders excluding transport up 0.6% after 0.4%, and nondefense capital goods excluding aircraft up 0.5% after 0.2%. That composition matters after Thursday's labor and housing figures gave little indication of an abrupt aggregate slowdown.

The final September Michigan survey the same day brings an immediate check on the expectations risk raised by Hammack and Barkin. Consensus is 47.6 for sentiment, against the previous 51.7, with one-year inflation expectations at 4.6% versus 4% and five-year expectations at 3.4% versus 3.3%. Weaker confidence alongside higher expected inflation would describe a different pressure on households from the resilience visible in recent activity readings. August core PCE on September 30 then provides a more direct inflation observation; forecasts call for 0.3% monthly and 3.4% annual increases, after 0.2% and 3.3%.

Energy diplomacy now turns on the proposed sequencing of Hormuz reopening and removal of the U.S. blockade. The latest improvement in LNG movements and Saudi sales has not prevented another large oil increase. A workable agreement would have to sustain physical flows despite the threat of wider military action. In early Asian trading Friday, before 7:15 a.m. Taipei, New Zealand bonds were already falling and Australian bond futures signaled further losses, carrying Thursday's pressure into the next session.

Issuer-specific deadlines remain consequential alongside the macro releases. Braskem was expected to put a new counteroffer before its board Friday, according to Valor Economico's Pipeline, with matched shareholder capital now an explicit Petrobras condition. Waskita's guarantee claim has a 20-business-day settlement window. Hong Kong's potential Monday digital-bond pricing and the Philippines' September 29 retail auction will establish financing terms in markets confronting higher global yields, while Hurricane Polo's evolving path will determine whether Mexico's contingent insurance protection is activated.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury selloff deepens as rising oil and resilient demand reinforce inflation concerns
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries extended their selloff on September 24, with the 10-year yield rising 8 basis points to 5.20% in late trading and the 30-year approaching 5.5%, its highest since 2004. The Treasury bought $4.08 billion of long-dated securities against a $6 billion ceiling, disappointing investors, while a $44 billion 7-year auction cleared at 5.085%, the highest yield since the maturity returned in 2009. Both real yields and inflation compensation rose; the pressure was not uniform across the curve, as the 2-year yield edged lower.

Brent finished the fixed-income session at $106.45, up 3.27%. Discussion of a phased Hormuz reopening briefly reduced oil's gains but did not reverse them. Initial jobless claims of 197,000 and new-home sales of 684,000 reinforced evidence of resilient demand. John Williams called expectations of another Fed increase by year-end reasonable, while Anna Paulson said modest further tightening could be appropriate; swaps fully priced three quarter-point increases over the following year.

The adjustment spread beyond Treasuries. At 3 p.m. New York time, 30-year municipal yields reached 5.07% as selling and withdrawals intensified. Norway raised its policy rate to 4.5%, and Bank of England deputy governors Sarah Breeden and Clare Lombardelli moved closer to supporting tightening, although second-round energy effects had developed more slowly than expected. U.S. equities recovered most of their intraday losses, leaving the most pronounced pressure in longer-duration fixed income.
overall_summary.summary: A smaller-than-expected Treasury buyback and a costly 7-year auction compounded pressure on longer maturities, while municipal yields climbed above 5% and European policymakers strengthened their tightening signals.
